notes:
One red beat, and it is Paul preaching on Mars' hill — not Jesus. Acts is Luke
writing, and the only red in Acts is where the risen Christ himself speaks, which
does not happen in chapter seventeen. So:

  p1  Acts 17:28  'For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also
      of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.'  RED -> SCRIPTURE

One line out of red into light blue. Red here made it sound as though Jesus were
quoting Greek poets to Athenians, which nobody would find in a red-letter Bible.

LIFTED FROM PARAPHRASE:
  s23  Acts 17:23  NEW (scripture). n0b already put the altar 'To the unknown God' on
       screen and then let the moment pass in modern English. Paul's actual answer to
       that altar is the hinge of the whole sermon, so it is now spoken verbatim on
       ST2, the altar still, with n1 following as its retelling exactly as written.

No splits — both quoted segments are Paul from end to end. Acts 17:23 and 17:28 are
quoted from the King James text as printed; nothing left as paraphrase from
uncertainty.

WHY-LAW: milk. Paul did not open by telling Athens it was wrong. He told them the God
they had been reaching for without a name had been near them the entire time — and
that they are his children. That is as gentle an on-ramp as scripture gets.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Paul stood in the middle of Athens, surrounded by statues to every god they could think of —

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and one altar that simply said, To the unknown God.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The one you already worship without knowing his name, Paul told them — that is the one I have come to tell you about. He told them they were already closer than they knew. The God they'd left unnamed made the whole world, and He is not far from any of us.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In Him, Paul said, we live and move and have our being. He even quoted their own poets: we are His children.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Everything you are, you are inside him — and even your own writers said it: we come from him. God overlooked the times of ignorance before, Paul said — but now He commands all men everywhere to repent.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The unknown God was never unknown to Him. He had been near the whole time.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You were made to be His. Reach out — He is not far.

stills_wanted.ST2: ST2 now carries the altar and Paul's answer to it — two beats, white then light blue, over one image. Frame the moment of the words: the plain stone altar with its inscription in the foreground and Paul beside it, one hand toward it, mid-sentence, addressing men who are out of frame. He should read as respectful, not triumphant — he is naming something they built, not knocking it over. Athens light, weathered stone, no crowd of hecklers.
